title: Sherry Wood:
title_short: Sherry Wood (CASS client) · This Place Saved My Life
headline: Sherry worked her whole life in management, and at 67 she had nowhere to go; CASS saved her life, and she found friends for life there.
story: Cold open on the fall: nowhere to go, no family, nowhere to stay. Then who she is: 68, from California, in Arizona 35 years.
She breaks the stereotype at once: she always worked, in management, often two jobs. At 67 she still ended up here.
Turn: this place saved her life, and she is grateful every day. Button: the people she met here are friends for life, everyday people like you. Composed and grateful, never pity.
do: Open cold on <q>I found myself</q> with the hook text on screen at 0:00.
Name super after the hook: <q>Sherry Wood · 68 · CASS client</q>.
Start <q>It's the most</q> without <q>Just that</q>, and cut her stutter under B-roll.
Take out the four shots Atdhe marked <q>remove this b roll</q> on Frame.io (23 Oct). Use only the B-roll on this page.
End card with the line <q>For more information visit cassaz.org</q>.
dont: Never label her Vista Colina. She is on the downtown (main) campus.
No sobriety or relapse lines (01:20 to 01:32 in the clip).
No unconfirmed place names (the transcript writes <q>Respero</q> at 01:12 and 02:13).
No dinner, drone or Vista Colina B-roll. No logo before the end card.

files: CASS Williams Family Community Dinner Production Brief
Nick's editor brief on the Monday item (5 Aug), plus Atdhe's Frame.io notes (11 Aug to 23 Oct). This page carries them.
CASS Shoot July 2026 raw · Sherry Client Interview · Downtown Shelter B Roll
Work Sans. CASS Navy #2C2B77, CASS Green #26B485, CASS Blue #006C9F, CASS Purple #7E3F98, Light Neutral #EEEEF1.
Soft, hopeful, no lyrics. Cleared against YouTube and Facebook claims.
tech: 20260727_C4470.MP4: 1920×1080, 23.976 fps in visual.json (check the camera file on import). Lav into the camera.
16:9 to 9:16, centred on Sherry. Check every B-roll crop by eye: no frames were pulled this run.

Atdhe flagged four spots: a strange sound on <q>years</q> (the join after <q>68 years old,</q>), a quiet part, an echo, and an audio overlap. Use 2-frame crossfades and room tone at every join, lift quiet words with clip gain, and make sure no second track plays under her voice.
-14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP peak. Music under the voice.
Pauses over 0.7 s inside a bite are cut to about 0.25 s.
Burned in, Work Sans, white #FFFFFF on the CASS navy #2C2B77 box, max 2 lines. CASS in capitals.
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920, 9:16. Upload to Frame.io, then Ready for Review.
checklist: Frame 1 is Sherry talking, with <q>I had nowhere to stay.</q> already on screen. No logo, name or fade.
Name super from 00:09: Sherry Wood · 68 · CASS client.

Captions read: <q>I found myself, nowhere to go</q>, <q>Divorced, again, and</q>, <q>My name is</q>, <q>in management positions.</q>, <q>oftentimes two.</q>, <q>but at 68 years old,</q>, <q>And this place saved my life.</q>, <q>Every day, I thank God,</q>, <q>It's the most</q>, <q>I've ever met, I've met here.</q>
No <q>Just that</q>, no stutter, no <q>incognito</q>, no health story.
The four shots Atdhe marked on Frame.io (23 Oct) are gone.
No Vista Colina, drone or dinner B-roll.
Every join is smooth: no strange sound on <q>years</q>, no echo, no second track.
End card: CASS logo with <q>For more information visit cassaz.org</q>.

client_note: Why this matters: Sherry is CASS's founding story in one person: a woman who always worked and still had nowhere to go at 67. CASS wants her composed and grateful, never pitied.

transcript:
Machine transcript of Sherry's interview (word times from the shoot's transcript.json). Times are mm:ss.s in the clip. The interviewer's questions are in the same file. Two place names in it are not confirmed and stay out of the cut.

[00:00.0] question is just tell me your name, your age, where are you from? [do not use: interviewer]
[00:03.7] My name is Sherry Wood.
[00:05.4] I'm 68 years old,
[00:08.1] incognito, [do not use: aside about her age]
[00:09.5] and I'm from California originally, but I've been out here for about 35 years.
[00:14.2] I came out here to raise my son, put him in better schools, and here I am.
[00:18.5] I would consider you a native now. [do not use: interviewer]
[00:20.5] What was your life like before you came to CASS? [do not use: interviewer]
[00:23.7] You know, I've always worked.
[00:26.4] I've always been in management positions, so I was usually working at least one job, oftentimes two.
[00:34.8] So busy, busy, busy, busy.
[00:36.8] And what is one way CASS has changed your life? [do not use: interviewer]
[00:40.4] You mean saved my life?
[00:42.5] Because that's when it's done.
[00:44.1] I don't even remember how I got to this point in my life, but at 68 years old, I was 67 when I got here,
[00:52.3] I found myself nowhere to go, no family out here, divorced again, and I had nowhere to stay.
[01:01.4] And I happened to get to CASS through an hip surgery when I got out of the hospital, told my doctor, hey, I don't know where I'm going. [do not use: hip surgery story, not needed]
[01:12.2] And so they actually took me over to Respero. [do not use: place name not confirmed]
[01:14.8] This place has been amazing.
[01:16.9] It's saved my life.
[01:18.7] It's kept me off the streets.
[01:20.8] Yeah, I was sober for a long time, but I was like teetering, just, I was just going through a lot. [do not use: health information, needs her sign-off]
[01:26.2] And so I like to think that it saved me from, you know, maybe even a relapse. [do not use: health information, needs her sign-off]
[01:31.4] I don't know. [do not use: health information, needs her sign-off]
[01:32.0] But I had no one, nowhere to go, nowhere to turn.
[01:35.5] And this place saved my life.
[01:37.9] I'm so grateful for it.
[01:39.3] Every day I thank God.
[01:40.8] And what would you want someone who supports CASS to know about your journey? [do not use: interviewer]
[01:45.8] I'm sorry? [do not use: interviewer]
[01:46.9] What would you want someone who supports CASS to know about your journey? [do not use: interviewer]
[02:03.9] Just that it's the most amazing place I've ever been.
[02:07.2] Like I said, I had nowhere to go, no one to turn to.
[02:11.2] And at my age, it's pretty frightening.
[02:13.4] And I ended up, I went to Respero first, went out for hip surgery. [do not use: place name not confirmed]
[02:18.8] And when I came back after a couple months, I made it over here to the main campus.
[02:24.5] And I was like really kind of spooked at first.
[02:28.3] It's a lot of people here from all walks of life,
[02:31.2] but I was amazed to find that some of the most amazing people I've ever met, I've met here.
[02:37.3] And they'll be friends for life.
[02:39.2] You know, they're just everyday people like you, like myself, like staff members.
[02:45.3] You know, they just, all it takes unfortunately is a couple of unfortunate events that can happen to anybody and you can be in a position where you have nowhere to go.
[02:55.2] This place saved my life.
[02:56.9] And if you had to look yourself in the mirror and give yourself encouragement, what would you say to yourself? [do not use: interviewer]
[03:04.2] You know, it's about putting one foot in front of the other.
[03:07.1] You can't give up.
[03:08.0] This life doesn't allow for that.
[03:11.1] I mean, people that give up, they end up in bad places.
[03:15.6] Places like this exist for people like me that are no different than you or anyone else.
[03:21.5] You know, like I said, one or two unfortunate events and you can find yourself without a place to stay.
[03:27.0] No home, no friends that can really help, no family.
[03:31.9] And it's a frightening place to be, but I came here and I met some of the most amazing people I've ever known in my life.
[03:40.5] People that I'll probably have in my life forever.
[03:42.6] Staff, other clients, and I'm just grateful.
[03:45.9] Every day I praise God for leading me here because I have learned so much.
[03:50.3] Like a lot of people, I had opinions before I ever stayed here.
[03:54.4] I'd see out front the way it looks and these people just are lazy, don't want to work.
[04:00.3] No, they're people just like I am that just had some unfortunate things happen.
[04:05.6] And you know, next thing you know you find yourself in a really dark place.
[04:11.3] This place is light in the middle of darkness.
[04:13.8] I'm grateful.
[04:15.1] Awesome. [do not use: crew talk]
[04:15.7] Thank you so much. [do not use: crew talk]
[04:16.8] You're welcome. [do not use: crew talk]
[04:17.6] It's my pleasure. [do not use: crew talk]
[04:18.5] I'm happy to do it.
